name: CompTIA CySA+ (V4)
note: CompTIA scores CySA+ on a 100–900 scale with 750 to pass. This practice exam reports a straight percentage; treat 85% as your readiness bar. The real exam also includes performance-based questions (PBQs), which this practice exam doesn't include, so practice hands-on analysis separately. Questions follow the CS0-004 exam objectives (version 2.0).

questions.stem: Logs from several servers show events in the wrong order, making it hard to build an incident timeline. What should be fixed first?
questions.explanation: Without consistent time synchronization, such as NTP, timestamps from different sources can't be correlated reliably. Retention and dashboards don't fix ordering problems.

questions.stem: An attacker who gains admin rights on a log server could delete evidence. Which logging practice best addresses this?
options: Forward logs to a protected central store
Store logs only on the local server's disk
Increase the logging verbosity on that server
Rotate the log files more frequently
questions.explanation: Protecting log integrity means sending logs off the host to a central, access-controlled, ideally immutable store so a compromised system can't erase them.

questions.stem: A company must keep firewall logs for one year to meet a regulation. Which logging concept does this describe?
questions.explanation: Retention defines how long logs are kept, often driven by legal, regulatory, or investigative needs. Ingestion is how logs are collected into a platform.

questions.stem: A SIEM isn't receiving events from newly deployed web servers. Which logging concept most likely needs attention?
questions.explanation: Ingestion covers how sources send logs to the SIEM, such as agents, forwarders, or syslog targets. New sources must be configured before events arrive.

questions.stem: Which Linux file would an analyst review to look for unauthorized accounts?
questions.explanation: /etc/passwd lists local user accounts, and /etc/shadow holds their password hashes. New or unexpected entries can indicate persistence.

questions.stem: An analyst sees a process named svch0st.exe running from a user's temp folder. Why is this suspicious?
options: Executables can't run from temporary folders
Windows never runs processes from any folder
Legitimate services always have long names
It mimics a system process from an odd path
questions.explanation: Malware often mimics system process names, such as svchost.exe, with small spelling changes and runs from unexpected locations. Legitimate svchost.exe runs from System32.

questions.stem: What is a key security concern with containers compared with virtual machines?
options: Containers can't be scanned for flaws
Containers always run as separate hardware
questions.explanation: Containers share the host operating system kernel, so a kernel exploit or container escape can affect the host and other containers. VMs are isolated by a hypervisor.

questions.stem: Which architecture gives remote users access to specific applications only after verifying identity and device posture for each request?
options: A flat network behind NAT and a firewall
questions.explanation: ZTNA brokers access to individual applications based on identity, device, and context, rather than placing users on the whole network as a traditional VPN does.

questions.stem: An organization wants to combine networking and security services, such as SWG, CASB, and ZTNA, in a cloud-delivered model. What is this called?
options: A demilitarized zone (DMZ) with a proxy
questions.explanation: SASE converges WAN networking with cloud-delivered security services so users get consistent protection wherever they connect.

questions.stem: Administrators must check out credentials for a short time, with sessions recorded, before managing critical servers. Which solution provides this?
options: Single sign-on (SSO) for all user accounts
A separate guest network for administrators
questions.explanation: PAM tools vault privileged credentials, grant time-limited access, and record sessions, reducing standing privilege and improving accountability.

questions.stem: A developer stores database passwords in environment files committed to a repository. What should replace this practice?
options: A longer password in the file
A private Git branch for the file
questions.explanation: Secrets managers store, rotate, and audit access to credentials, and applications retrieve them at runtime. Encoding isn't encryption, and private branches still expose secrets.

questions.stem: Which industrial system collects data from remote sites, such as pipelines, and lets operators control equipment centrally?
questions.explanation: Supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems monitor and control geographically distributed industrial processes, such as utilities and pipelines.

questions.stem: Why are many operational technology (OT) systems difficult to monitor with standard endpoint agents?
options: They are always located in the public cloud
They use only encrypted wireless connections
They run legacy software that can't host agents
They don't produce any network traffic at all
questions.explanation: OT devices often run legacy or vendor-specific systems where agents aren't supported or could affect safety. Passive network monitoring is commonly used instead.

questions.stem: Which data protection concept ensures that sensitive data is unreadable if a laptop is stolen?
questions.explanation: Encryption at rest, such as full-disk encryption, protects stored data on lost or stolen devices. Encryption in transit protects data moving across networks.

questions.stem: A company enrolls corporate phones so it can enforce passcodes and remotely wipe lost devices. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: MDM enforces policies, such as encryption, passcodes, and app controls, and supports remote lock and wipe for mobile devices.

questions.stem: Which practice reduces a server's attack surface before it goes into production?
questions.explanation: System hardening removes unnecessary services and accounts, applies secure settings, and follows benchmarks such as CIS, reducing exploitable weaknesses.

questions.stem: A workstation is sending large volumes of outbound traffic to an unfamiliar IP address at 3 a.m. What does this most likely indicate?
questions.explanation: Unusual outbound transfers to unknown destinations, especially off-hours, are a classic exfiltration indicator. Analysts should verify against known backup or sync jobs.

questions.stem: Firewall logs show one internal host connecting to ports 1–1024 on every address in a subnet. What activity is this?
questions.explanation: Sequential connections to many ports and hosts indicate scanning and enumeration, often an attacker mapping the network after initial access.

questions.stem: A host makes small HTTPS requests to the same external domain every 60 seconds, around the clock. What does this pattern suggest?
options: A user streaming a long training video
questions.explanation: Regular, periodic connections with consistent sizes are typical of malware beaconing to a C2 server. Jitter may be added, but the regularity often remains visible.

questions.stem: An analyst finds a web server listening on TCP 4444, which isn't part of its approved configuration. Which indicator is this?
questions.explanation: Services on unexpected ports, such as 4444, which is commonly used by Metasploit listeners, can indicate backdoors or reverse shells.

questions.stem: An attacker uses certutil.exe to download a payload from the internet. Which type of indicator does this represent?
options: Rogue device on the wired network
questions.explanation: LOLBins are legitimate, signed system tools, such as certutil, mshta, or rundll32, that attackers abuse to download or run code while blending in.

questions.stem: A server's CPU usage is at 100% for days, and an unfamiliar process is connecting to a mining pool. What is the likely cause?
options: A memory leak in the OS
questions.explanation: Unexplained high resource consumption with connections to mining pools indicates cryptojacking, where attackers use compromised resources to mine cryptocurrency.

questions.stem: File integrity monitoring alerts that system binaries in the Windows System32 folder changed outside a patch window. What does this suggest?
options: Expected browser cache and cookie activity
questions.explanation: Unexpected changes to critical system files can indicate malware, rootkits, or tampering. Analysts should compare hashes against known-good versions.

questions.stem: A sign-in from London is followed 15 minutes later by one from Sydney for the same account. Which indicator is this?
questions.explanation: Impossible travel flags sign-ins from locations too far apart to be reached in the time between them, suggesting credential compromise. VPNs can cause false positives.

questions.stem: Users receive links to paypa1-secure.com. Which social engineering technique is being used?
questions.explanation: Typosquatting registers look-alike domains with small misspellings, such as replacing "l" with "1", to trick users into visiting malicious sites.

questions.stem: Why are URL shorteners a concern in phishing investigations?
options: They block email filtering tools completely
They hide the real destination of a link
They can only be opened on mobile devices
questions.explanation: Shortened URLs obscure the final destination, so users and some filters can't see that a link leads to a malicious site. Analysts expand them safely before visiting.

questions.stem: A finance employee receives an email from what appears to be the CEO's account, requesting an urgent wire transfer to a new vendor. What attack is most likely?
questions.explanation: BEC uses compromised or spoofed executive or vendor accounts to trick employees into sending money or data. Out-of-band verification of payment changes is a key control.

questions.stem: A cloud account suddenly launches dozens of GPU instances in an unused region. Which indicator is this?
questions.explanation: Unexpected resource creation, especially in unused regions, often means stolen cloud credentials used for cryptomining or other abuse.

questions.stem: A service account that normally reads one database begins querying every table and exporting results. What should the analyst suspect?
questions.explanation: Behavior outside an account's normal pattern, such as broad queries and exports, suggests the account's credentials are being misused.

questions.stem: A web application becomes unavailable, and logs show thousands of requests per second from many IP addresses. Which indicator is this?
options: A DDoS attack disrupting the service
questions.explanation: A flood of requests from many sources causing unavailability is consistent with a distributed denial-of-service attack.

questions.stem: An unknown device with a MAC address from a consumer router vendor appears on a switch port in the server room. What is this?
questions.explanation: Rogue devices are unauthorized hardware connected to the network. They can bypass controls or provide attacker access and should be located and removed.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to decode a Base64-encoded, gzip-compressed PowerShell payload. Which tool is designed for this?
questions.explanation: CyberChef chains operations, such as Base64 decoding, decompression, and XOR, to decode and analyze data quickly.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to capture packets on a headless Linux server from the command line. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: tcpdump captures and filters packets from the command line and can write pcap files for later analysis in Wireshark.

questions.stem: Which tool produces rich, structured logs of network activity, such as connections, DNS queries, and HTTP requests, rather than signature alerts?
questions.explanation: Zeek (formerly Bro) is a network security monitor that generates detailed protocol logs for analysis. Snort and Suricata focus on signature-based detection.

questions.stem: A team wants a signature-based network IDS/IPS that supports multithreading and inspects traffic at high speed. Which tool fits best?
questions.explanation: Suricata is a multithreaded IDS/IPS engine that uses signature rules, many of which are compatible with Snort, and can also log protocol metadata.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to check whether an IP address has been reported for malicious activity by other organizations. Which tool helps most?
questions.explanation: AbuseIPDB collects community reports of abusive IP addresses, giving reputation context during investigations.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to find who registered a suspicious domain and when. Which tool provides this?
questions.explanation: WHOIS lookups show domain registration details, such as registrar and creation date. Recently registered domains are often suspicious.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to see readable text, such as URLs and IP addresses, embedded in a suspicious binary without running it. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: The strings utility extracts printable character sequences from files, often revealing URLs, commands, or messages without executing the sample.

questions.stem: A team wants to write rules that match malware families based on byte patterns and strings in files. Which tool is used?
questions.explanation: YARA rules describe patterns, such as strings and byte sequences with conditions, to identify and classify malware across files and memory.

questions.stem: An analyst submits a file hash to see whether dozens of antivirus engines detect it. Which service is this?
questions.explanation: VirusTotal checks files, hashes, URLs, and domains against many antivirus engines and reputation sources. Uploading files can expose sensitive data, so hashes are often checked first.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to run a suspicious attachment and observe its behavior, such as file changes and network calls, in isolation. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Sandboxes such as Cuckoo or Joe Sandbox execute samples in isolated environments and report their behavior.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to check a domain's SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records and see whether its mail server is on blocklists. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: MXToolbox performs DNS and email diagnostics, including SPF, DKIM, and DMARC lookups and blocklist checks.

questions.stem: Which capability baselines normal behavior for users and devices and alerts on deviations, such as unusual sign-in times?
questions.explanation: UEBA builds behavioral baselines and flags anomalies that may indicate compromised accounts or insider threats.

questions.stem: Which platform lets organizations share threat indicators and events in a structured way with trusted communities?
questions.explanation: The Malware Information Sharing Platform (MISP) stores and shares indicators and events, supporting collaborative threat intelligence.

questions.stem: An analyst needs to find every log line containing an IPv4 address. What should they use?
questions.explanation: Regular expressions match text patterns, such as IP addresses, emails, or hashes, across logs and data.

questions.stem: A command line shows: powershell -nop -w hidden -enc JABjAGwA... What should the analyst conclude?
options: It's a standard Windows update command
It only lists files in the current folder
It runs a hidden, encoded command, which is suspicious
It's a harmless network connectivity diagnostic
questions.explanation: -nop skips the profile, -w hidden hides the window, and -enc runs a Base64-encoded command, all common in malicious PowerShell. Decoding the payload reveals intent.

questions.stem: Windows event logs exported for analysis use which native file format?
questions.explanation: Windows stores event logs in the binary EVTX format, viewable in Event Viewer or parsed by tools and SIEMs.

questions.stem: A cloud provider's audit logs are structured as nested key-value pairs in braces and brackets. Which format is this?
questions.explanation: JSON uses objects in braces and arrays in brackets, and it's common for cloud and API logs. Analysts often parse it with tools such as jq or Python.

questions.stem: Which tool family monitors endpoints, records process and file activity, and can isolate a compromised host?
questions.explanation: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools collect endpoint telemetry, detect threats, and support actions such as host isolation. XDR extends this across more sources.

questions.stem: An analyst writes a script to pull IoCs from an API and compare them with local logs on Windows servers. Which language is native to Windows administration?
questions.explanation: PowerShell is Windows' native scripting language for administration and automation. Python and shell scripts are also common for security tasks.

questions.stem: A well-funded group maintains long-term, stealthy access to a target's network to steal intellectual property. Which threat actor is this?
questions.explanation: APTs are sophisticated, often state-linked actors that pursue long-term, targeted campaigns and work to remain undetected.

questions.stem: According to the Pyramid of Pain, which indicator is hardest for an attacker to change once defenders detect it?
options: File hashes of their malware samples
questions.explanation: TTPs sit at the top of the Pyramid of Pain because changing behavior is costly. Hashes and IPs are at the bottom because they're trivial to change.

questions.stem: A team colors MITRE ATT&CK techniques by how often they appear in recent incidents. What is this visualization called?
questions.explanation: Heat maps over ATT&CK show technique frequency or coverage, helping teams prioritize detections and hunts.

questions.stem: Which factor reduces confidence in a threat intelligence report about an indicator?
options: It came from a trusted partner
It is specific to your industry
It matches activity in your logs
The indicator is several years old
questions.explanation: Timeliness, relevance, and accuracy drive confidence. Old indicators, such as IPs, may have changed owners and are less likely to be useful.

questions.stem: Which source is an example of closed-source threat intelligence?
questions.explanation: Closed-source intelligence comes from proprietary or restricted sources, such as paid feeds or private sharing groups. OSINT is publicly available.

questions.stem: What is the difference between atomic and behavioral indicators of compromise?
options: Atomic describe patterns; behavioral are single values
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
Atomic come only from network logs; behavioral from endpoints
Atomic are single values; behavioral describe activity patterns
questions.explanation: Atomic IoCs, such as an IP, hash, or domain, can't be broken down further. Behavioral IoCs describe patterns, such as a process spawning a shell and then connecting outbound.

questions.stem: Using STRIDE, an attacker changes the amount field in a transaction request. Which threat category is this?
questions.explanation: Tampering is unauthorized modification of data. Spoofing is impersonation, repudiation is denying an action, and elevation of privilege is gaining higher access.

questions.stem: In STRIDE, an attacker uses another user's session token to act as that user. Which category is this?
questions.explanation: Spoofing involves pretending to be another user or system. Strong authentication and session protection mitigate it.

questions.stem: A team proactively searches for signs of an attacker's technique that existing alerts wouldn't catch. What is this activity?
questions.explanation: Threat hunting is hypothesis-driven searching for threats that evade automated detection, often guided by threat intelligence and ATT&CK techniques.

questions.stem: A company deploys fake file shares and decoy credentials that alert when touched. Which concept is this?
questions.explanation: Cyber deception uses decoys, such as honeypots, honeytokens, and fake shares, to detect attackers, since legitimate users have no reason to access them.

questions.stem: Analysts conclude that an attack was carried out by a specific group based on its tools, infrastructure, and techniques. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Attribution links activity to a threat actor using TTPs, infrastructure, and other evidence. It's often uncertain and should be expressed with confidence levels.

questions.stem: A SOC wants to automatically enrich phishing alerts, block malicious senders, and open tickets without analyst clicks. Which platform fits?
questions.explanation: Security orchestration, automation, and response (SOAR) platforms run playbooks that integrate tools and automate repetitive response steps.

questions.stem: A SIEM rule generates hundreds of false positives daily from a vulnerability scanner. What should the team do?
options: Tune the rule to exclude the scanner
questions.explanation: Rule tuning reduces noise by adding exclusions or thresholds for known benign activity, so analysts can focus on real threats.

questions.stem: Adding geolocation and reputation data to IP addresses in alerts is an example of what?
questions.explanation: Enrichment adds context, such as threat intel, asset owner, or GeoIP, to alerts, speeding triage and improving decisions.

questions.stem: A ticketing system needs to notify a SOAR platform immediately when a new incident is created. Which integration method fits?
questions.explanation: Webhooks send HTTP callbacks when events occur, enabling near-real-time integration between tools. APIs and plug-ins are other integration methods.

questions.stem: Why should a SOC create documented playbooks for common incident types?
options: They eliminate the need for any training
They make responses consistent and repeatable
They replace the incident response plan
They prevent all incidents from occurring
questions.explanation: Playbooks and runbooks standardize steps, reduce errors, help coordination across shifts, and form the basis for automation.

questions.stem: A SOC manager wants leadership to see alert volume, open incidents, and response times at a glance. What should be built?
questions.explanation: Dashboards visualize key operational metrics for different audiences, supporting oversight and decision-making.

questions.stem: An analyst uses an AI assistant to summarize an incident, but it cites a log entry that doesn't exist. Which AI risk is this?
questions.explanation: Hallucinations are confident but false outputs. Analysts must verify AI-generated findings against the source data.

questions.stem: Analysts paste customer PII and internal logs into a public AI chatbot. Which risk does this create?
questions.explanation: Sensitive data shared with external AI services may be stored or used outside the organization's control. Approved tools and AI usage policies reduce this risk.

questions.stem: A log file being summarized by an AI tool contains text instructing the AI to ignore suspicious entries. Which risk is this?
questions.explanation: Malicious prompts, including indirect prompt injection hidden in analyzed data, can manipulate AI output. AI-assisted analysis must be validated.

questions.stem: What should an organization establish before allowing analysts to use generative AI tools?
questions.explanation: AI usage policies define approved tools, allowed data, review requirements, and compliance obligations, supporting governance of AI in the SOC.

questions.stem: Which task is a strong use case for AI in security operations?
options: Correlating events across large log sets
questions.explanation: AI can help correlate events, summarize logs, compare artifacts, and draft documents, but humans should validate outputs and make high-impact decisions.

questions.stem: Before starting a vulnerability management program, what must an organization have so it knows what to scan?
options: A list of approved AI tools
A complete set of SIEM dashboards
questions.explanation: You can't assess what you don't know about. An asset inventory defines scan scope, ownership, and criticality.

questions.stem: Scans of production database servers have caused slowdowns during business hours. Which planning consideration should change?
questions.explanation: Scheduling scans outside peak hours, or throttling them, reduces performance impact on operations.

questions.stem: A scanner on the internet is used to see what an attacker outside the network could find. What type of scan is this?
questions.explanation: External scans assess internet-facing exposure from an outsider's view. Internal scans assess systems from inside the network.

questions.stem: Laptops are often off the corporate network, so scheduled network scans miss them. Which approach helps most?
questions.explanation: Agents installed on endpoints assess them locally and report results whenever they connect, covering remote and intermittently connected devices.

questions.stem: Why does a credentialed scan usually produce fewer false positives than a non-credentialed scan?
options: It can inspect installed software and patch levels directly
It uses only external DNS records to identify systems
It reports only the vulnerabilities rated critical
It skips any host that requires authentication
questions.explanation: Credentialed scans log in and read actual versions and configurations instead of inferring them from banners, improving accuracy.

questions.stem: An ICS network can't tolerate active probing. Which scanning approach is safest?
options: Full port scans during peak production
questions.explanation: Passive scanning observes traffic to identify devices and vulnerabilities without sending probes that could disrupt fragile OT systems.

questions.stem: A team wants to identify which hosts are live and what operating systems they run before detailed scanning. Which scan type is this?
options: Static code analysis of the apps
questions.explanation: Discovery scans map live hosts and use device fingerprinting to identify operating systems and services, informing later vulnerability scans.

questions.stem: A retailer must regularly scan systems that store cardholder data and have external scans done by an approved vendor. Which standard requires this?
questions.explanation: PCI DSS requires internal and external vulnerability scans, with external scans performed by an Approved Scanning Vendor (ASV).

questions.stem: A team scans servers against prescriptive, consensus-based hardening settings, such as password policy and disabled services. What are these baselines?
questions.explanation: CIS Benchmarks provide secure configuration baselines for operating systems, applications, and cloud services that scanners can check against.

questions.stem: A scanner on the user network can't reach servers in a restricted VLAN. Which planning consideration explains this?
questions.explanation: Network segmentation and firewall rules can block scanners, so scanners may need placement in each segment or firewall exceptions.

questions.stem: Which scan type sends probes to hosts and services and may affect system performance?
questions.explanation: Active scans interact with targets directly, giving detailed results but adding load. Passive scans only observe existing traffic.

questions.stem: Nmap output shows: 22/tcp open ssh OpenSSH 7.2p2. What can the analyst conclude?
options: The host is running an HTTP web server on port 22
SSH is blocked by a firewall on the host
SSH is open, and that old version may be vulnerable
The scan confirms that SSH has been exploited
questions.explanation: An open port with a version banner shows the service is reachable. Old versions, such as OpenSSH 7.2, should be checked against known vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: Which Nmap option performs service version detection?
questions.explanation: -sV probes open ports to identify service versions. -sn is a ping sweep without port scanning, -Pn skips host discovery, and -oX writes XML output.

questions.stem: Nmap reports a port as "filtered." What does this mean?
options: A firewall or filter is blocking the probes
The service is open and accepting connections
The port is closed and responding with resets
questions.explanation: Filtered means Nmap can't tell whether the port is open because packets are being dropped or blocked, usually by a firewall.

questions.stem: A team needs to scan the entire IPv4 internet range for one open port as fast as possible. Which tool is built for this?
questions.explanation: Masscan is an extremely fast asynchronous port scanner designed for large address ranges.

questions.stem: A penetration tester wants to confirm that a vulnerability is exploitable by running a known exploit module. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Metasploit provides exploit modules, payloads, and post-exploitation tools to validate vulnerabilities in authorized testing.

questions.stem: An analyst wants to visualize relationships between a company's domains, email addresses, and employees from public sources. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Maltego performs OSINT link analysis and graphs relationships among entities, such as people, domains, and infrastructure.

questions.stem: Which tool is a modular, command-line framework for web-based reconnaissance, similar in style to Metasploit?
questions.explanation: Recon-ng uses modules to gather OSINT, such as hosts and contacts, through a Metasploit-like console.

questions.stem: A tester needs to intercept and modify HTTP requests between a browser and a web application. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Burp Suite works as an intercepting proxy for manual web testing and includes a scanner. OWASP ZAP is a free alternative.

questions.stem: Which tool quickly scans web servers for dangerous files, outdated server software, and misconfigurations?
questions.explanation: Nikto is a web server scanner that checks for known dangerous files, outdated versions, and server configuration issues.

questions.stem: A team wants a fast scanner driven by community YAML templates to check for specific CVEs across many hosts. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Nuclei runs template-based checks, written in YAML, for vulnerabilities and misconfigurations at scale.

questions.stem: Which open-source tool is a full-featured network vulnerability scanner often used as an alternative to Nessus?
questions.explanation: OpenVAS (part of Greenbone) is an open-source vulnerability scanner with a large feed of network vulnerability tests.

questions.stem: A team wants to audit an AWS account against CIS benchmarks for misconfigurations, such as public S3 buckets. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Prowler assesses AWS (and other cloud) environments against security best practices and compliance frameworks. ScoutSuite is a multi-cloud alternative.

questions.stem: Developers want to scan container images for vulnerable packages before deployment. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Trivy scans container images, file systems, and IaC for known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.

questions.stem: A team wants to catch insecure settings in Terraform templates before infrastructure is deployed. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Checkov performs static analysis of infrastructure as code, such as Terraform and Kubernetes manifests, to find misconfigurations.

questions.stem: A SOC wants to safely emulate specific ATT&CK techniques to test whether its detections fire. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Atomic Red Team provides small, technique-mapped tests that validate detections. Breach and attack simulation tools such as Caldera automate adversary emulation.

questions.stem: Which tool is an automated adversary emulation platform from MITRE?
questions.explanation: MITRE Caldera automates adversary emulation using ATT&CK techniques, supporting breach and attack simulation and purple teaming.

questions.stem: A web scanner reports a possible SQL injection, but manual testing shows the input is safely parameterized. How should this finding be classified?
questions.explanation: A false positive is a reported issue that doesn't actually exist. Validating findings prevents wasted remediation effort.

questions.stem: A CVSS 9.8 vulnerability is on an isolated lab server, and a CVSS 7.5 vulnerability is being actively exploited on an internet-facing server. Which should be fixed first?
options: Neither until a full audit is complete
The 9.8 because its base score is higher
Both at the next quarterly patch window
questions.explanation: Prioritization should weigh active exploitation, exposure, and asset value, not only CVSS base score. An exploited, exposed system carries more real risk.

questions.stem: What does the Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) estimate?
options: The severity of a vulnerability's technical impact
The cost to remediate a vulnerability
The number of assets affected by it
The probability a vulnerability will be exploited soon
questions.explanation: EPSS estimates the likelihood that a vulnerability will be exploited in the next 30 days, complementing CVSS severity in prioritization.

questions.stem: In a CVSS vector, AV:N means what?
questions.explanation: AV is attack vector, and N is network, meaning it's remotely exploitable. PR is privileges required, AC is attack complexity, and A is availability impact.

questions.stem: Which CVSS base metric describes whether a user must take an action, such as clicking a link, for exploitation?
questions.explanation: User interaction (UI) indicates whether exploitation requires a victim's participation. Requiring interaction lowers the score.

questions.stem: A vulnerability exists on a server that can only be reached from a segmented, isolated network. How does this context affect prioritization?
options: It has no effect on how the finding is prioritized
It may lower priority because exposure is limited
It raises priority above all internet-facing systems
It means the vulnerability can be ignored permanently
questions.explanation: Context awareness considers whether a system is internal, external, or isolated. Limited reachability reduces likelihood, though the finding still needs tracking.

questions.stem: A scanner missed a vulnerability that later turned out to exist on a server. What is this called?
questions.explanation: False negatives are real issues the tool didn't detect. They are dangerous because they create a false sense of security.

questions.stem: A critical vulnerability has no patch yet. The team adds a WAF rule and restricts access to the system. What is this?
questions.explanation: Compensating controls reduce risk when the primary fix isn't available, until a patch can be applied.

questions.stem: A business owner can't patch a legacy app until next year. The risk is documented, approved by management, and set for review. What is this?
questions.explanation: Exceptions document why a vulnerability won't be fixed on schedule, who approved it, compensating controls, and when it will be reviewed.

questions.stem: After a patch is deployed, what should the team do before closing the vulnerability ticket?
questions.explanation: Validation of remediation, usually by rescanning or testing, confirms that the vulnerability is actually resolved.

questions.stem: An organization continuously discovers and monitors its internet-facing assets, including forgotten subdomains. Which mitigation strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Attack surface management identifies and reduces exposed assets, such as unknown hosts, shadow IT, and stale DNS records, that attackers could target.

questions.stem: Which secure coding practice prevents SQL injection?
questions.explanation: Parameterized queries separate code from data so input can't change query structure. Client-side validation alone is easily bypassed.

questions.stem: A code scan flags a file inclusion flaw where user input sets a path to a file already on the server. What is this vulnerability called?
questions.explanation: LFI lets attackers include local files, such as configuration or log files, through unsanitized input. RFI includes files from a remote URL.

questions.stem: Which scenario describes the impact criterion in vulnerability prioritization?
options: How easy it is to write exploit code for the flaw
How many scanners detected the vulnerability
How much harm exploitation would cause the business
How long the vendor took to release a patch
questions.explanation: Impact measures the consequences to confidentiality, integrity, availability, and the business if the vulnerability is exploited.

questions.stem: A security awareness policy that requires annual training is which control type?
questions.explanation: Administrative (managerial) controls are policies, procedures, and training. Technical controls are implemented in systems, and physical controls protect facilities.

questions.stem: Which control function does an EDR's automatic isolation of an infected host perform?
questions.explanation: Responsive controls act when an incident is detected to limit its impact. Preventative controls stop incidents before they happen.

questions.stem: After compensating controls are applied, some risk from a vulnerability remains. What is it called?
questions.explanation: Residual risk is what remains after controls. Inherent risk is the level before any controls are applied.

questions.stem: Leadership states that it will accept only low risks for customer-facing systems. What does this statement define?
questions.explanation: Risk appetite is the amount and type of risk an organization is willing to pursue or retain to meet its objectives.

questions.stem: A company buys cyber insurance to cover the costs of a breach. Which risk management strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Transferring shifts financial impact to a third party. The organization still owns the risk and must manage it.

questions.stem: A company decommissions a vulnerable legacy FTP service rather than securing it. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Avoidance removes the risk by eliminating the activity or system that creates it.

questions.stem: A policy states that critical vulnerabilities must be remediated within 15 days. What does this target define?
questions.explanation: Remediation timelines are service-level objectives (SLOs) set by policy and governance, often tracked as KPIs and SLAs.

questions.stem: Which testing method analyzes source code for vulnerabilities without running the application?
questions.explanation: Static application security testing examines source or compiled code early in development. DAST tests the running application from the outside.

questions.stem: A scanner sends crafted requests to a running web application in staging to find vulnerabilities. Which method is this?
questions.explanation: Dynamic application security testing interacts with the running application, finding issues such as injection and misconfigurations at runtime.

questions.stem: An organization wants a framework to assess and improve its software security practices across the development life cycle. Which model fits?
questions.explanation: The Software Assurance Maturity Model (SAMM) helps organizations measure and improve secure software practices across governance, design, implementation, verification, and operations.

questions.stem: A newly disclosed flaw affects a popular open-source logging library. Which tool helps find every application that uses it?
questions.explanation: SCA tools inventory third-party and open-source components and their versions, flagging known vulnerable dependencies.

questions.stem: What does a software bill of materials (SBOM) provide?
options: A list of components and versions in software
A list of employees who wrote the code
A record of all licenses the company has bought
A schedule of planned software releases
questions.explanation: An SBOM inventories software components and dependencies, helping organizations quickly assess exposure to newly disclosed vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: A vendor's software update was compromised and pushed malware to customers. Which risk category does this represent?
questions.explanation: Supply chain risk arises from third-party vendors, software, and services. SBOMs, vendor assessments, and code signing checks help manage it.

questions.stem: A missing patch on a public web server has a CVSS of 8.1, no known exploit, and no patch available yet. Which criterion most limits the remediation options?
questions.explanation: When no patch exists, teams must rely on mitigations, such as compensating controls, until the vendor releases a fix.

questions.stem: In the Cyber Kill Chain, an attacker sends a phishing email with a malicious attachment. Which phase is this?
questions.explanation: Delivery is when the weapon reaches the target, such as by email, web, or USB. Weaponization is building the payload, and reconnaissance is gathering information.

questions.stem: In the Cyber Kill Chain, malware establishes a channel to an attacker-controlled server for remote instructions. Which phase is this?
questions.explanation: Command and control (C2) gives the attacker remote control of the compromised system. It follows installation and precedes actions on objectives.

questions.stem: An attacker pairs an exploit with a backdoor to create a deliverable payload before sending it. Which Kill Chain phase is this?
questions.explanation: Weaponization combines an exploit with a payload, such as a malicious document. It happens on the attacker's side before delivery.

questions.stem: What are the four core features of the Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis?
questions.explanation: The Diamond Model links adversary, capability, infrastructure, and victim for each event, helping analysts pivot between related activity.

questions.stem: An analyst finds a C2 domain and searches for other victims communicating with the same infrastructure. Which model describes this pivoting?
questions.explanation: The Diamond Model encourages pivoting between features, such as from infrastructure to other victims or capabilities, to expand an investigation.

questions.stem: How does MITRE ATT&CK differ from the Cyber Kill Chain?
options: ATT&CK applies only to cloud environments
ATT&CK details specific techniques per tactic
ATT&CK covers only the reconnaissance and delivery phases
ATT&CK is a vulnerability scoring system for patches
questions.explanation: The Kill Chain is a high-level, linear model. ATT&CK is a detailed knowledge base of real-world tactics and techniques, useful for detection mapping and hunting.

questions.stem: In MITRE ATT&CK, what does a "tactic" represent?
options: A vulnerability score for an exploit
The adversary's goal, such as persistence
A single indicator, such as a file hash
A specific tool, such as Mimikatz or PsExec
questions.explanation: Tactics are the "why," such as initial access or lateral movement. Techniques are the "how," the specific methods used to achieve each tactic.

questions.stem: An attacker uses stolen credentials and RDP to move from a workstation to a file server. Which ATT&CK tactic is this?
questions.explanation: Lateral movement covers techniques for moving through the environment after initial compromise, such as remote services with valid accounts.

questions.stem: Building the IR team, buying forensic tools, and writing playbooks happen in which incident response phase?
questions.explanation: Preparation establishes the plans, people, tools, and training needed to respond before an incident occurs.

questions.stem: A SIEM alert is reviewed and confirmed as a real intrusion. Which phase does this belong to?
questions.explanation: Detection identifies potential incidents from alerts, reports, and monitoring. Analysis then determines scope, severity, and impact.

questions.stem: An analyst determines which systems are affected, how the attacker got in, and what data was accessed. Which phase is this?
questions.explanation: Analysis investigates the scope, cause, and impact of an incident to guide containment and eradication decisions.

questions.stem: Malware is removed and compromised accounts are reset after systems are isolated. Which phase is this?
questions.explanation: Eradication removes the threat, such as malware, persistence, and attacker accounts, and fixes the root cause.

questions.stem: Cleaned systems are restored from backups, monitored closely, and returned to production. Which phase is this?
questions.explanation: Recovery restores normal operations, validates systems, and monitors for signs of reinfection.

questions.stem: Why is containment usually performed before eradication?
options: To stop the incident from spreading while it's removed
To delete evidence before the investigation starts
To restore every system from backup immediately
To notify customers before scoping the incident
questions.explanation: Containment limits damage and spread, buying time to investigate and plan eradication without the attacker expanding access.

questions.stem: Which phase includes reviewing what happened, documenting lessons learned, and updating plans?
questions.explanation: Post-incident activities capture lessons learned, root causes, and improvements to controls, playbooks, and training.

questions.stem: Which document defines who's on the IR team, their authority, and how incidents are handled across the organization?
questions.explanation: The IR plan defines scope, roles, responsibilities, severity levels, and procedures, and is supported by playbooks for specific incident types.

questions.stem: Which document specifies how and when the IR team informs executives, legal, PR, and external parties during an incident?
options: A change request for the CAB
questions.explanation: Communication plans define stakeholders, channels, approval, and timing for internal and external communication, including out-of-band methods.

questions.stem: The IR team walks through a simulated ransomware scenario in a meeting without touching systems. What is this?
questions.explanation: Tabletop exercises are discussion-based walkthroughs that test plans, roles, and decisions. Simulations involve more realistic, hands-on activity.

questions.stem: Why should incident roles, such as incident commander and communications lead, be defined in advance?
options: So legal never needs to be involved
So incidents can't be escalated later
So responsibilities are clear under pressure
So no one needs any training afterward
questions.explanation: Predefined roles avoid confusion, duplicated effort, and gaps in decision-making during an incident.

questions.stem: An analyst receives 40 alerts at once and must decide which to investigate first. What is this process called?
questions.explanation: Triage assesses alerts for validity, severity, and urgency so the most critical issues are handled first.

questions.stem: An analyst links a firewall log, a proxy entry, and an EDR alert that all share the same host and time window. What is this?
questions.explanation: Correlation connects related events across sources to reveal the full picture of an attack. SIEMs automate much of this.

questions.stem: Analysts add asset owner, criticality, and threat intel reputation to raw logs during an investigation. What is this?
options: Log rotation and compression on each host
questions.explanation: Enrichment adds context to log data, making it faster to judge severity and decide next steps.

questions.stem: Why is building a timeline important during an investigation?
options: It shows the sequence of attacker actions
It determines the attacker's legal identity
It replaces the need to collect evidence
questions.explanation: Timelines order events from multiple sources, revealing initial access, dwell time, lateral movement, and the scope of compromise.

questions.stem: A compromised server holds regulated customer data and supports a revenue-critical service. What should this most directly influence?
questions.explanation: Determining severity and impact considers data sensitivity, business criticality, and scope, which drive prioritization and escalation.

questions.stem: Why do investigators hash a disk image immediately after acquiring it?
options: To encrypt the image for secure storage
To compress the image to save space
To remove deleted files from the image
To prove later that the image hasn't changed
questions.explanation: Data integrity validation compares hashes over time to show evidence wasn't altered, supporting its admissibility.

questions.stem: What does a chain of custody document?
options: The list of vulnerabilities found in a scan
The attacker's movement through the network
The order of systems restored after an incident
Who handled evidence, when, and why
questions.explanation: Chain of custody records every transfer and access to evidence, which is essential for its integrity and legal use.

questions.stem: Legal counsel instructs IT to suspend automatic deletion of emails related to an incident because litigation is likely. What is this?
questions.explanation: A legal hold preserves relevant data that would otherwise be deleted, ensuring it's available for legal proceedings.

questions.stem: An infected workstation should be investigated, but the attacker must not reach other systems. What should be done first?
options: Power it off immediately at the switch
Wipe and reimage it at once
questions.explanation: Network isolation, for example through EDR, stops spread while preserving volatile memory and evidence for analysis. Powering off loses RAM contents.

questions.stem: Why might an analyst capture memory before shutting down a compromised host?
options: Memory capture removes malware from the host
Memory holds volatile evidence lost at shutdown
Memory is the only place that logs are stored
Shutting down automatically deletes the disk
questions.explanation: RAM can contain running processes, network connections, encryption keys, and fileless malware that disappear when the system powers off.

questions.stem: An L1 analyst confirms an intrusion on a domain controller beyond their authority to handle. What should they do?
options: Close the ticket as a false positive
Escalate per the incident response plan
Wait for the next shift to review it
questions.explanation: Escalation moves incidents to higher tiers or leadership based on severity and defined criteria, ensuring the right expertise and authority are involved.

questions.stem: After eradication, how should the team confirm a host is clean before releasing it from isolation?
options: Verify remediation with scans and monitoring
Ask the user if the computer seems faster
Assume it's clean after a single reboot
Check that the host still powers on
questions.explanation: Remediation and verification confirm malware and persistence are gone and vulnerabilities are fixed before reconnecting the host.

questions.stem: What should happen before a remediated server is reconnected to the production network?
options: Verify it's clean, then release it with monitoring
Delete all logs from the isolation period
Reconnect it immediately to minimize downtime
Disable monitoring on it to reduce alert noise
questions.explanation: Release from isolation should follow validation and include heightened monitoring to detect any reinfection.

questions.stem: A team restores a database from the last backup taken before the compromise. Which activity is this?
questions.explanation: Restoration returns systems and data to a known-good state, using clean backups or rebuilt images, before resuming operations.

questions.stem: An investigation finds that an unpatched VPN appliance allowed initial access. What has the team identified?
questions.explanation: Root cause analysis finds the underlying reason an incident happened so corrective actions prevent recurrence.

questions.stem: After the RCA, the team creates a plan to patch all VPN appliances within 48 hours of future advisories. What is this?
questions.explanation: Corrective actions address root causes and gaps found during the incident, with owners and deadlines to prevent repeat incidents.

questions.stem: Which type of evidence should generally be collected first, according to the order of volatility?
questions.explanation: Collect the most volatile data first: registers and cache, then memory and network state, then disk, and finally remote and archival data.

questions.stem: Why should investigators work on a forensic copy rather than the original drive?
options: To avoid altering the original evidence
Because copies are always faster to read
To skip the chain of custody process
questions.explanation: Analyzing a verified copy preserves the original's integrity. Write blockers prevent changes during acquisition.

questions.stem: An alert from the EDR tool should automatically page the on-call analyst for critical severities. Which IR technique does this support?
questions.explanation: Alerting and notification rules make sure the right people are informed quickly based on severity, enabling timely response.

questions.stem: Several incidents are active at once with limited staff. What should determine which is handled first?
options: The order in which the alerts arrived
questions.explanation: Prioritization focuses limited resources on incidents with the greatest potential impact on critical assets, data, and operations.

questions.stem: Which training method most realistically tests a team's technical response by injecting real-looking attack activity into a test environment?
questions.explanation: Simulations exercise tools and procedures hands-on. Tabletops are discussion-based and test decisions and coordination.

questions.stem: Why should playbooks be created for common incident types, such as phishing and ransomware?
options: They replace the overall incident response plan
They give responders tested, step-by-step actions
They remove the need for incident escalation
They guarantee every incident is prevented
questions.explanation: Playbooks provide consistent, repeatable steps for specific scenarios and can be automated in SOAR.

questions.stem: An investigator needs to gather endpoint logs, firewall logs, and cloud audit logs into one place for the investigation. What is this activity?
questions.explanation: Log collection centralizes relevant data so it can be correlated and analyzed, ideally before retention limits remove it.

questions.stem: During an investigation, the team suspects an insider. Who should usually be involved before interviewing the employee?
questions.explanation: Insider cases have employment and legal implications, so HR and legal guide interviews, evidence handling, and actions.

questions.stem: Ransomware has encrypted file servers. Which containment step is most appropriate first?
options: Delete all backups to prevent reinfection
Pay the ransom to get the decryption key
Isolate affected systems and block spread
questions.explanation: Isolating infected systems and blocking lateral movement paths, such as SMB, limits spread. Backups must be protected, not deleted.

questions.stem: A phishing email reached 300 users. What's an efficient containment step?
options: Reset every user's password in the company
Purge the message and block the sender
Disable email for the entire company for a week
Ask each user to forward the message to IT
questions.explanation: Purging the message, blocking the sender and URLs, and checking who clicked limits further exposure without disrupting the business.

questions.stem: Which artifact helps show when a program was executed on a Windows system?
questions.explanation: Windows Prefetch records program execution, including run counts and timestamps, which helps build timelines.

questions.stem: Which data integrity validation method should be used for evidence?
questions.explanation: Cryptographic hashes such as SHA-256 detect any change to evidence. File names and sizes can stay the same after tampering.

questions.stem: An organization wants analysts to preserve evidence in a way that keeps it usable in court. Which practice is most important?
options: Analyzing evidence on the original drive
Sharing evidence on public file shares
questions.explanation: Preservation requires proper acquisition, hashing, secure storage, and chain of custody so evidence remains admissible.

questions.stem: An attacker scrapes a company's job postings and LinkedIn profiles to learn its technologies and staff names. Which Kill Chain phase is this?
questions.explanation: Reconnaissance gathers information about the target before an attack. Defenders have limited visibility here, but OSINT reviews can reduce what's exposed.

questions.stem: A user opens a malicious document, and a flaw in the word processor runs the attacker's code. Which Kill Chain phase is this?
questions.explanation: Exploitation is when the vulnerability is triggered to run attacker code. Installation then establishes persistence on the system.

questions.stem: Detection engineers map their SIEM rules to ATT&CK techniques and find that no rules cover credential dumping. What has this exercise revealed?
questions.explanation: Mapping detections to ATT&CK shows which techniques are covered and which aren't, guiding new detection development and hunts.

questions.stem: Which report lists each discovered vulnerability with its affected hosts, severity, and remediation guidance?
options: A shift handover note for the SOC
questions.explanation: Scan reports detail findings for technical teams, including affected assets, severity, evidence, and recommended fixes.

questions.stem: An auditor finds that the company didn't remediate critical vulnerabilities within the timeframe required by PCI DSS. What is this?
questions.explanation: Compliance findings document gaps against regulatory or contractual requirements and usually require corrective action plans.

questions.stem: Leadership wants a simple view that grades each business unit's vulnerability exposure as red, amber, or green. What should the team provide?
questions.explanation: Risk scorecards summarize risk in an easy-to-compare format for non-technical audiences and help drive accountability.

questions.stem: A vulnerability can't be fixed until a vendor updates a dependent component. Where should this be captured?
options: In the chain of custody form
questions.explanation: Action plans list remediation steps, owners, deadlines, dependencies, and escalation paths so blocked items are visible and managed.

questions.stem: A contract with a hosting provider prohibits the customer from patching the provider-managed OS. Which inhibitor to remediation is this?
questions.explanation: Contracts and SLAs can limit who may change systems and when. Remediation must be coordinated with the responsible party.

questions.stem: Patching a manufacturing control system would require stopping the production line for two days. Which inhibitor is this?
questions.explanation: When remediation would interrupt critical business processes, it may be delayed to planned downtime, with compensating controls in place meanwhile.

questions.stem: Testing shows that a security patch breaks a key feature of a line-of-business application. Which inhibitor is this?
questions.explanation: Patches that degrade or break functionality may be postponed while vendors fix the issue, with risk documented and mitigated.

questions.stem: A critical system runs software whose vendor went out of business, so no patches will ever be released. Which inhibitors apply?
questions.explanation: Legacy or proprietary systems often lack patches or vendor support. Isolation, compensating controls, and replacement planning are needed.

questions.stem: Every change to production must be approved by a change board that meets monthly, delaying urgent patches. Which inhibitor is this?
questions.explanation: Governance processes, such as change approvals, can slow remediation. Emergency change procedures help with critical vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: Why should the vulnerability management team identify stakeholders for each system?
options: So the scanner's license costs are reduced
So the right owners receive findings and act on them
So results can be shared publicly on the website
So scans can skip systems with no named owner
questions.explanation: Stakeholder identification ensures system owners, IT teams, and leadership get relevant information and are accountable for remediation.

questions.stem: A CISO wants to know whether the number of open critical vulnerabilities is rising or falling each quarter. Which metric fits?
questions.explanation: Trend metrics show progress and emerging problems over time, which is more meaningful to leadership than a single snapshot.

questions.stem: Which vulnerability metric shows whether teams fix issues within the agreed remediation timeframes?
questions.explanation: SLA compliance measures the percentage of vulnerabilities remediated within the defined window for their severity.

questions.stem: A report for executives highlights the ten vulnerabilities posing the greatest business risk. Which KPI concept is this?
questions.explanation: Top-risk reporting focuses leadership attention on the most significant exposures and the decisions or resources they need.

questions.stem: A critical vulnerability has missed its remediation deadline twice, and the system owner isn't responding. What should the team do?
questions.explanation: Escalation paths in action plans move overdue critical items to management so they get attention and resources.

questions.stem: How should vulnerability findings be presented to a non-technical board?
options: As a full raw scanner export
In terms of business risk and trends
As a list of every CVE identifier
questions.explanation: Executives need concise information about business risk, trends, and required decisions, not technical detail.

questions.stem: Which of these is an inhibitor to remediation rather than a remediation step?
questions.explanation: Patch availability is an inhibitor. When no fix exists, teams rely on compensating controls until one is released.

questions.stem: Who should formally declare that an event has become an incident?
options: The external auditor at the next audit
The attacker, by sending a ransom note
The person or role authorized in the IR plan
Any employee who reads about the event
questions.explanation: IR plans define who can declare incidents and set severity, which triggers escalation, communications, and resources.

questions.stem: What should an incident executive summary focus on?
options: Full packet captures from the network
Every command run by the analysts
The source code of the malware sample
questions.explanation: Executive summaries give leadership a concise view of impact, risk, actions taken, and decisions or resources required.

questions.stem: During a breach investigation, which team should review public statements before they're released?
questions.explanation: Legal ensures statements meet obligations and don't create liability, and PR manages messaging and reputation.

questions.stem: A breach exposed residents' personal data, and state law requires notice within a set timeframe. Who must the company notify besides customers?
questions.explanation: Many laws require notifying regulators, such as state attorneys general or data protection authorities, within specific deadlines.

questions.stem: When should law enforcement be involved in an incident?
options: Only after all evidence is deleted
Never, because it always slows recovery
As the plan defines, guided by legal
questions.explanation: The communication plan, with legal counsel, defines when to engage law enforcement, such as for extortion, fraud, or criminal intrusions.

questions.stem: The attacker may be monitoring corporate email. How should the IR team communicate?
options: Through a public social media group
By posting updates on the intranet
questions.explanation: Operational security requires secure, out-of-band communication channels so attackers can't see response activity.

questions.stem: Which document describes what happened during an incident, what went well, and what should improve?
questions.explanation: After action reports document the incident, timeline, response effectiveness, root cause, and lessons learned.

questions.stem: An analyst's shift ends during an active incident. What should they do?
options: Close the incident to keep metrics clean
Escalate everything to the CISO to reset
Leave without notes; logs show everything
Hand over status, findings, and open tasks
questions.explanation: Shift handovers transfer context, actions taken, pending tasks, and evidence locations so the response continues smoothly.

questions.stem: A threat intelligence team writes a report explaining how a new ransomware campaign could affect the company's specific systems. What makes this an internal threat intelligence report?
options: It lists every global CVE released this year
It's copied from a public news article
It's written only for external customers
It's tailored to the company's environment
questions.explanation: Internal threat intelligence reports translate external threats into specific relevance, risk, and recommended actions for the organization.

questions.stem: Which metric measures the average time between when an intrusion begins and when the SOC identifies it?
questions.explanation: MTTD measures how long threats go unnoticed. Lower MTTD limits attacker dwell time.

questions.stem: Which metric measures how quickly the SOC begins acting on incidents after they're detected?
questions.explanation: Mean time to respond tracks the time from detection to containment or response actions.

questions.stem: A SOC's alerts are 90% false positives, and analysts are overwhelmed. Which metric highlights this problem?
questions.explanation: A high false-positive rate signals the need for rule tuning and better detection logic to reduce alert fatigue.

questions.stem: Which metric reflects how many alerts turn out to be genuine malicious activity?
questions.explanation: The true-positive rate shows detection quality. Rising rates indicate rules are well tuned to real threats.

questions.stem: Which metric measures the share of employees who clicked links in simulated phishing emails?
questions.explanation: Phishing click rates show awareness program effectiveness and help target training.

questions.stem: A SOC manager tracks the total number of alerts generated per day to plan staffing. Which metric is this?
questions.explanation: Alert volume helps with capacity planning and can reveal noisy detections or changes in threat activity.

questions.stem: Which metric measures the average time from opening an incident ticket until it's fully resolved and closed?
questions.explanation: Mean time to close covers the full incident life cycle through documentation and closure.

questions.stem: During an incident, which stakeholder needs to be told when services will be restored, without technical details?
questions.explanation: Customer communication focuses on impact, timelines, and actions they should take, coordinated with legal and PR.

questions.stem: Why should root cause analysis be included in post-incident reporting?
options: So the incident can be closed faster
So corrective actions address the real cause
So the attacker can be identified by name
So legal holds can be lifted earlier
questions.explanation: Including the root cause ensures improvements target underlying weaknesses, preventing similar incidents.
